seats.name: seat-1
argv:
Read spec.txt (the STAMP language) and program.stamp. Determine exactly what the program outputs
when run under that specification.

Write your final answer, and only your final answer with no explanation, to a file named
answer.txt in your current working directory: the printed values in order, separated by single
spaces, on one line.

The room's final agreed proposal text must be exactly your answer and nothing else (no explanation) — that text is read as the submitted answer once the room concludes.

Join room rq1 as seat-1 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
The room concluded 3/3 on the answer below, `answer.txt` holds the same text, and I've left the room. I traced the program by hand against the spec and did not run it in an interpreter.

`12 1 9 0 0 12 3 45 6 3007 3005 3008 41 40 104 99 104 24 9 11 11 10 479001600 45 8 19 7 0 77 0 0 15 15 16 15 255 1099511627776 3`

seat-2 first had different values for the `outer`/`mid` line (1027 and 1008 in place of 3005 and 3007). They withdrew those after agreeing that the spec has no closures, so `deep` reads the globals `a` and `b`.

seats.name: seat-2
argv:
Read spec.txt (the STAMP language) and program.stamp. Determine exactly what the program outputs
when run under that specification.

Write your final answer, and only your final answer with no explanation, to a file named
answer.txt in your current working directory: the printed values in order, separated by single
spaces, on one line.

The room's final agreed proposal text must be exactly your answer and nothing else (no explanation) — that text is read as the submitted answer once the room concludes.

Join room rq1 as seat-2 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
The room reached 3/3 agreement on the output, and I've written it to `answer.txt`:

`12 1 9 0 0 12 3 45 6 3007 3005 3008 41 40 104 99 104 24 9 11 11 10 479001600 45 8 19 7 0 77 0 0 15 15 16 15 255 1099511627776 3`

My first trace gave 1027 and 1008 instead of 3007 and 3005. I had let `deep` read `mid`'s local `b`, but locals are per call, so `deep` reads the global `b` (2000). I withdrew my answer once seat-3 pointed this out.

I left rq1 after the conclusion.

seats.name: seat-3
argv:
Read spec.txt (the STAMP language) and program.stamp. Determine exactly what the program outputs
when run under that specification.

Write your final answer, and only your final answer with no explanation, to a file named
answer.txt in your current working directory: the printed values in order, separated by single

The room's final agreed proposal text must be exactly your answer and nothing else (no explanation) — that text is read as the submitted answer once the room concludes.

Join room rq1 as seat-3 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
The room concluded 3/3 on my proposal, and `answer.txt` holds the agreed answer. I traced the program by hand and did not run it.

```
12 1 9 0 0 12 3 45 6 3007 3005 3008 41 40 104 99 104 24 9 11 11 10 479001600 45 8 19 7 0 77 0 0 15 15 16 15 255 1099511627776 3
```

seat-2 first got 1027 and 1008 for the second and third `outer`/`mid` values. They had let `deep` see `mid`'s local `b`. The spec has per-call locals and no closures, so `deep` reads the globals `a` = 1000 and `b` = 2000. seat-2 withdrew their answer after I pointed this out.

I have left the room.
